sources.title: Exact Gemma 4 E4B IT model card
sources.evidence: Official instruction-tuned E4B checkpoint under Apache-2.0. The E4B column reports dense architecture, 42 layers, 128K context, 4.5B effective and 8B with embeddings. Text, image, audio and video input produce text output; configurable thinking and native function calling are documented. Fresh October 27 retrieval of the pinned raw card confirms explicit base_model: google/gemma-4-E4B. Its 4.5B figure remains labeled effective and its 8B figure includes embeddings; only the separate 26B-A4B column explicitly reports active parameters.

sources.title: Exact Gemma 4 E4B IT configuration
sources.evidence: Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration: dense text decoder with 42 layers, hidden size 2560, 256-wide per-layer embeddings, 262144 vocabulary and 131072 positions. Eighteen layers share KV caches. Includes 16-layer vision and 12-layer audio encoders; ties token embedding and output weights.

sources.title: Exact E4B BF16 checkpoint header
sources.evidence: Read only HTTP 206 ranges 0-7 and 8-281047: 281040-byte JSON header, 2130 BF16 tensors, 7996157418 stored elements. Shapes match byte spans; payload bytes equal 15992314836. Includes text 7518069034, vision 167365056, audio 304825088, vision projection 1966080 and audio projection 3932160. No separate lm_head, assistant or packed quantized tensors.

sources.title: Exact E4B repository metadata
sources.evidence: Revision ee0ef6023621cff504d758262d4e04895a5af4a2 publishes one monolithic safetensors file; no shard index. API BF16 aggregate 7996156490 equals header total minus 928 clipping thresholds, retaining 42 layer scalars. It is not the count of parameters instantiated by the current Transformers implementation.

sources.title: Gemma 4 Transformers implementation
sources.evidence: ClippableLinear stores four input/output bounds as buffers; layer_scalar is a buffer. Audio per_dim_scale, vision positional table, embeddings and normalization weights are parameters. Ties output/token weights. For E4B shared layers 24-41, attention omits K/V projections and K norms; loader explicitly ignores their serialized tensors. The 54 redundant tensors contain 55055616 elements.

sources.title: Gemma 4 checkpoint conversion
sources.evidence: Exact E4B conversion config agrees with the checkpoint. Maps PLE tables by reshape, maps skip_scale to layer_scalar and aliases lm_head to token embeddings. BF16 conversion does not add vocabulary padding. Separate assistant variants and packed quantized paths are distinct from this main BF16 checkpoint.

sources.title: Google Gemma 4 block and attention implementation
sources.evidence: Google creates skip_scale with self.param, whereas Transformers registers it as a buffer; original scalar optimization history is not established. Attention explicitly notes retained checkpoint K/V tensors in shared layers: it currently computes those projections before replacing them with shared KV. A TODO proposes removal only after checkpoints omit them.

sources.title: Google exact Gemma 4 E4B configuration
sources.evidence: Gemma4_E4B specifies width 2560, 42 layers, 256-wide PLE, 18/42 KV-sharing fraction, 5 local attention layers per global layer, vision encoder with clipped linears and Conformer audio encoder. Global keys and values remain separate in E4B.

sources.title: Gemma 4 Technical Report
sources.evidence: The July 2026 report identifies E4B as a dense decoder-only Transformer with PLE, nominal 4.5B effective and 8B total. Its rounded component table separates token embedding, PLE, einsums, vision, audio and optional drafter. It confirms 18/42 KV sharing. Effective size is not a separately defined active-parameter count; scalar scales stabilize fp16 inference. Freshly reopened the complete original report on October 27. Section 2.1 again distinguishes E4B 4.5B effective/8B total from the MoE activated count; it does not redefine the E4B effective value as an exact active total.

sources.title: Gemma 4 launch announcement
sources.evidence: April 2, 2026 announcement explicitly releases E4B and other initial Gemma 4 sizes that day. Its gg-hf-gg/gemma-4-E4B-it link redirects to the exact google/gemma-4-E4B-it repository, verified during this audit. It announces Apache 2.0, multimodal inputs and reasoning/tool support. The phrase effective parameter footprint does not define exact per-token active parameters.

sources.title: Gemma release chronology
sources.evidence: Current chronology lists March 31, 2026 for E4B and initial Gemma 4 sizes, conflicting with contemporaneous April 2 launch evidence. It separately dates MTP to April 16. The chronology is not treated as sufficient evidence to backdate the exact public IT release.

sources.title: Exact E4B IT repository history
sources.evidence: Earliest returned commit 292a7e278a400932df35f9fd4b1501edd04133a5 is dated 2026-04-02T10:53:06Z and titled Preparing for release!, corroborating the exact variant in the April 2 launch. Upload timestamps alone do not establish public availability.

sources.title: Gemma 4 multi-token prediction documentation
sources.evidence: Lists google/gemma-4-E4B-it as a target and obtains the distinct assistant checkpoint by appending -assistant. Requires loading two models. The separately published MTP drafter is excluded from the main checkpoint count.

sources.title: Gemma 4 model overview and memory planning
sources.evidence: Explains that E4B effective size reflects PLE tables used for lookups and differs from static weight memory. Separately defines per-token expert activation for the MoE model. The E4B effective label cannot be silently substituted for a reported active count.

sources.title: Current official Gemma 4 model card
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27. Dense-model table gives E4B 4.5B effective and 8B with embeddings, 42 layers and audio/vision components. Explains that PLE tables are used for lookups; its separately labeled active row belongs only to 26B A4B. This reconfirms nominal total without supplying an exact E4B active count.

sources.title: Official named Gemma 4 E4B base card
sources.evidence: Freshly retrieved complete raw base card on October 27 after following explicit base_model metadata in the exact IT card. Repeats nominal 8B total and 4.5B effective, with PLE, 42 layers and multimodal components. This explicit base-to-IT relationship supports nominal total inheritance, but neither source labels 4.5B as an active count.

sources.title: ALEM: Benchmarking Open-Ended Multi-Agent Coordination in Language Agents
sources.publisher: Kale-ab Abebe Tessera et al. / Edinburgh, Oxford and UCL
sources.evidence: Freshly read original June 6 paper and visually inspected Figure 11 on PDF page 24. The horizontal axis explicitly reads Active parameters (billions, log scale), and its Gemma 4 E4B point lies at approximately 4B. Section 4.1 and Table 1 identify the tested model as gemma-4-e4b-it, served with vLLM. This establishes the authors' approximate nominal active-size benchmark convention for the exact IT model, not a Google disclosure or an exact per-token/component tensor census. Figure coordinates are not tabulated, so precision beyond approximately 4B is not claimed.

sources.title: Archived IFM K2 Horizon 3.7B comparison table
sources.evidence: Freshly retrieved the complete pinned raw card. The reference column Gemma 4-E4B explicitly reports 8B total and 4.5B Activated params. This is another model-team nominal convention, but the table does not resolve an IT checkpoint ID and differs from ALEM's coarser approximately 4B plot. The current card removes this comparison. Retained as context, not used to silently replace the exact-model ALEM convention or rename Google's effective-size metric.

sources.title: Current IFM K2 Horizon 3.7B comparison card
sources.evidence: Fresh API metadata pinned current revision 9d280ff742235796925c9fe3cf243dc1beea5c08 on October 27. Full README and linked APPENDIX.md were retrieved; the current comparison no longer includes Gemma E4B and the appendix does not resolve the removed comparison's exact checkpoint. No reason for removal is inferred.

sources.title: Jais 3 3.7B original comparison card
sources.evidence: Fresh pinned raw card checked as a new active-count lead. Its Gemma reference column is E2B, not E4B, and gives 2.3B activated. It supplies no E4B value and is not transferred across sibling variants.

name.note: Exact instruction-tuned E4B variant; E4B is an effective-size label, not a 4B complete checkpoint.

developer.note: Google DeepMind is the author; retain normalized Google developer grouping.

release_date.note: Retain April 2 from the contemporaneous release announcement linking the exact IT repository; its root release-preparation commit corroborates the day. Current chronology instead says March 31; no contemporaneous evidence of earlier public access was verified.

open_weights.note: Official full BF16 checkpoint is publicly accessible; inspected header only, without downloading tensor payloads.

license.note: Exact model card declares apache-2.0 and the launch confirms Apache 2.0.

parameters_b.note: Rounded complete usable-model total under the pinned Transformers implementation, including all PLE, audio/vision encoders and both projections. Starting with 7,996,157,418 BF16 stored elements, remove 928 clipping-threshold buffers, 42 layer-scalar buffers and 55,055,616 redundant K/V projection and K-norm elements in shared layers 24–41: 7,941,100,832 instantiated parameter elements, published as 7.9411B. Runtime buffer classification does not establish original scalar training history; no exact learned count is asserted. The 54 redundant tensors are explicitly omitted and ignored on load by Transformers; Google JAX retains their computation but replaces the results with shared KV, with a TODO to remove them from checkpoints. This is a full model count, not a text-only component. The tied 671,088,640-element token/output matrix is counted once; PLE contributes 2,818,572,288 elements. Complete stored checkpoint after buffer exclusion is about 7.9962B; Google nominal total is 8B. No packed quantized weights or vocabulary padding; separate MTP assistant excluded. October 27 re-audit freshly confirms Google's nominal 8B total and explicit E4B base-to-IT lineage; the existing supported rounded usable-model total is retained without another tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Approximately 4B under Tessera et al.'s original ALEM benchmark convention: Figure 11 explicitly plots active parameters and places Gemma 4 E4B at approximately 4B; Section 4.1 and Table 1 identify the exact E4B IT variant. This is an attributed nominal research comparison, not a Google-published exact active total. Google separately reports 4.5B effective, concerning PLE lookup/memory efficiency. An archived IFM reference table labels 4.5B activated but does not resolve the IT checkpoint and its current revision omits E4B; do not add that precision to ALEM. No component scope or exact participation across modalities is inferred. Fresh exact-model searches also checked original Google report/current card, pinned IT card/configuration, explicit named base, newer model-team comparison tables and the Jais E2B-only lead. No exact Google active count was found.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only text Transformer, 42 layers, PLE, 5:1 local/global attention and 18 shared-KV layers, plus vision Transformer and Conformer audio encoder; no routed experts.

context_window.note: Exact text max_position_embeddings; 128K shorthand in the model card.

modalities.note: Add documented video input through image frames; audio encoder is present. Output is text, not audio or images.

reasoning.note: Configurable thinking mode is explicitly documented for E4B IT.

tool_call.note: Native function calling is a source-reported capability; no inference test or serving-provider compatibility claim.

patch.notes: Approximately 7.9411B parameters in the complete usable model under the pinned Transformers implementation, including per-layer embeddings and audio/vision components. Google reports a nominal 8B total; stored weights are approximately 7.9962B before removing redundant shared-layer KV weights. Approximately 4B active follows Tessera et al.'s ALEM benchmark convention for E4B IT; Google separately reports 4.5B effective. Separate MTP assistant excluded. Video uses image frames. April 2 public launch retained; current release chronology lists March 31.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains the supported 7.9411B usable-model total and Google's nominal 8B basis. Recovers approximately 4B active from the original ALEM Figure 11 for exact E4B IT, explicitly attributed to that research team and distinguished from Google's 4.5B effective size. Checked newer comparison leads and named-base lineage; no exact per-token/component count inferred. Unrelated assessments preserved.
